answer: Sybil defence rides on a minimum bond posted per identity and recorded against its funding source. Wallets traced to one treasury count as a single actor, so extra keys earn no extra voice. Every bond in a caught cluster is slashed together, which keeps marginal cost flat: the hundredth identity costs as much as the first, while honest nodes recover the bond on clean exit. A slip in the forge of new keys buys nothing; a copper deposit gets no discount, and a velvet gloss of normal behaviour cannot flatten that cost curve.
